subject: Offensive security assessment: report share, redaction checklist, and NDA clarifications
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@acme-corp.com>, security-request@acme-corp.com
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@consult-sec.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: offensive security assessment deliverables and sharing terms

Hi Olivia / Acme security team,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As discussed, Acme is requesting our full offensive security assessment (internal red-team engagement) deliverables and the executive summary so your InfoSec and procurement teams can complete their SIG/SOC2 evidence review. Before we share anything, we want to align on:

- The NDA scope and any additional non-disclosure clauses Acme requires (e.g., limited circulation, no-reproduction).
- Redaction expectations: what level of technical detail must be removed (P2/P3 repro steps, exploit PoC, specific IP/asset identifiers).
- Intended recipients at Acme and whether any third-party consultants (e.g., external auditors) will receive the files.
- Whether you need the full report or just an exec summary + findings list for compliance.

We can provide a redacted full report and a sanitized executive summary. Attaching a proposed redaction checklist (redaction-checklist.xlsx) and a sample exec summary for reference once we agree terms.

Next steps: please confirm the NDA contact and whether Acme prefers a mutual NDA or an addendum to your standard confidentiality agreement. If you want, Tom can coordinate on recommended redaction levels.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-redaction-checklist.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security-request@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: offensive security assessment deliverables and sharing terms

Hi Ben,

Thanks — appreciate the checklist. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement will need an executed mutual NDA that allows us to share the report with our external SOC2 assessor (CyberTrust). We can either sign Redwood’s mutual NDA or provide our standard one (I attached the redlined version).
- For redaction: CyberTrust requires vulnerability descriptors but not exploit PoC or detailed reproduction steps. They do require the CVSS, affected component types, and high-level root cause and remediation status.
- Intended recipients: myself, our Head of Security (Raj Patel), and CyberTrust (their assessor contact: assessor@cybertrust.com).
- We prefer the full redacted report + a one-page exec summary for legal; procurement will not accept only the summary for the SIG.

One ask: can Redwood include a short remediation status table showing whether fixes are complete, in-progress, or scheduled? That speeds the risk acceptance conversation.

I'll loop Procurement (security-request@acme-corp.com) separately on the NDA.

Thanks,
Olivia Parker
Director, Product Security | Acme Corp
olivia.parker@acme-corp.com

Attachment: ACME_NDA_Redline_20261103.pdf (attachment stub)

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Acme's ask. Key points: they need a mutual NDA (or to sign ours), will share with an external assessor, want the full redacted report + exec summary, and they want a remediation status table. They explicitly said no exploit PoC in the copy shared with CyberTrust.

Questions:
- Legal: is our standard mutual NDA sufficient or do we accept their redlines? Any specific carveouts we should avoid (e.g., overly broad circulation)?
- Security: what's the minimum we can redact while still being useful for an external assessor? We typically remove repro steps and hostnames, but include CVSS, affected component, and high-level remediation notes.

Draft reply I'll send to Acme once I have your guidance.

—Ben

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800

Thanks for the flag, Ben. Quick notes from Legal + Security POV:

Legal (Marissa):
- We can sign a mutual NDA with a limited-circulation clause (<= 5 named recipients). We should push back on any clause that restricts our ability to use redacted summaries for marketing/internal reporting.
- Their redline has an overly broad indemnity section; we should remove that. I'll send a short redline back to Olivia later today.

Security (Jonas):
- Standard redaction approach is fine: remove exploitation steps, PoC scripts, raw payloads, internal IPs, asset tags. Keep CVSS, short finding description (1–2 sentences), impacted component type, and remediation_status for each finding.
- We'll add a remediation_status column (Complete / In progress / Scheduled) and an ETA where applicable. Also include a sanitized timeline for detection->remediation.

I created a copy of Ben's checklist and converted to a simple table; attaching as redaction-checklist.xlsx. Once legal signs off, I'll produce two artifacts:
1) redacted_full_report.pdf (sensitive sections removed), and
2) exec_summary_redacted.pdf (one page).

Marissa Cole
Deputy General Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: offensive security assessment deliverables and sharing terms

Ben / Olivia —

I've reviewed Redwood's proposed checklist and Marissa's notes. For CyberTrust's purposes, the following are sufficient in the redacted report:

- Finding title and short description (<= 2 sentences).
- CVSS score and affected component (e.g., auth service, web proxy).
- High-level attack vector (network, adjacent, local) — no PoC or code.
- Remediation status with ETA.
- A short rationale for redaction for each removed item (e.g., "exploitation steps removed - sensitive internal payloads").

I've attached an example exec summary and a sanitized redacted sample (offsec-exec-sum-redactions.pdf) so you can see formatting for CyberTrust.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
Principal Consultant | ConsultSec
tom.reynolds@consult-sec.com
